sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedant.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹坦。

sentences.en: Almost exactly a century ago, a British ship, the Endurance, became trapped in Antarctic sea ice.
sentences.zh: 几乎正好在整整一个世纪前，一艘名为“坚忍号”的英国船只被困在了南极的海冰中。

sentences.en: Aboard were 28 men, led by the explorer, Ernest Shackleton.
sentences.zh: 船上有28名船员，由探险家欧内斯特·沙克尔顿率领。

sentences.en: On October 27, 1915, the pressure of the ice crushed the keel of the Endurance.
sentences.zh: 1915年10月27日，冰层的压力压碎了“坚忍号”的龙骨。

sentences.en: Freezing water rushed in.
sentences.zh: 冰冷的江水汹涌而入。

sentences.en: The sailors dragged lifeboats and supplies from the ship onto the ice.
sentences.zh: 水手们把救生艇和补给品从船上拖到了冰面上。

sentences.en: Carrying the lifeboats, they started hiking toward open water.
sentences.zh: 他们带着救生艇，开始徒步寻找开阔水域。

sentences.en: After a week with little progress, Ernest Shackleton realized they would be better off
sentences.zh: 在进展甚微的一周之后，欧内斯特·沙克尔顿意识到，他们最好

sentences.en: camping on an ice floe and waiting for it to drift toward open water.
sentences.zh: 在冰上露营，等待冰块漂向开阔水域。

sentences.en: What followed was an extraordinary story of knowledge and resourcefulness.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一段关于知识与应变能力的传奇故事。

sentences.en: The explorers managed to get their lifeboats into the water and row to dry land,
sentences.zh: 探险队员们设法把救生艇放入水中，划行到了陆地上，

sentences.en: a place called Elephant Island.
sentences.zh: 一个叫做象岛的地方。

sentences.en: But the desolate island offered little by way of resources and no hope of rescue.
sentences.zh: 但这荒凉的岛屿几乎提供不了什么资源，也没有获救的希望。

sentences.en: So Ernest Shackleton and a smaller group took one of the lifeboats and set out for a whaling station.
sentences.zh: 于是欧内斯特·沙克尔顿和一小队人乘坐其中一艘救生艇出发前往一个捕鲸站。

sentences.en: It was 800 miles away.
sentences.zh: 那是800英里外。

sentences.en: Across seas were towering waves and deadly storMs.
sentences.zh: 穿过巨浪滔天、风暴致命的海域。

sentences.en: The explorers had only basic navigation equipment.
sentences.zh: 探险队员们只有最基础的导航设备。

sentences.en: Somehow, using the stars to guide them, they made it to the island of South Georgia.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，他们靠着繁星指引，最终到达了南乔治亚岛。

sentences.en: But storms had blown them to the wrong side of the island as the whaling station.
sentences.zh: 但风暴把他们吹到了岛屿与捕鲸站相反的一侧。

sentences.en: They now had to hike across the island, across frozen mountains and icy glaciers, to reach help.
sentences.zh: 为了寻求救援，他们现在必须徒步横穿该岛，跨越冰冻的山脉和冰川。

sentences.en: Ernest Shackleton eventually commanded a ship back to Elephant Island to rescue the remainder of his crew.
sentences.zh: 欧内斯特·沙克尔顿最终指挥一艘船返回象岛，营救了剩下的船员。

sentences.en: He saved every last man.
sentences.zh: 他救下了最后一个人。

sentences.en: This is the kind of story that is popular in novels and movies.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种在小说和电影里很受欢迎的故事。

sentences.en: The explorers came up with creative solutions to problems
sentences.zh: 探险队员们想出了应对问题的创意思路

sentences.en: and displayed a deep understanding of the challenges before them.
sentences.zh: 并对他们面临的挑战表现出了深刻的理解。

sentences.en: They kept their heads and saved themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们保持冷静，自救成功。

sentences.en: Stories like this obscure how much we understand about our own worlds.
sentences.zh: 像这样的故事掩盖了我们对自己世界的理解程度。

sentences.en: When we face obstacles, even simple problems like a punctured tire,
sentences.zh: 当我们面临障碍时，哪怕是像轮胎漏气这样简单的问题，

sentences.en: a malfunctioning phone, or an odd pain in our stomachs,
sentences.zh: 手机故障，或者肚子隐隐作痛，

sentences.en: are we any good at figuring out what to do?
sentences.zh: 我们真的擅长弄清楚该怎么做吗？

sentences.en: Closing the gap between what we know and what we think we know?
sentences.zh: 去缩小我们所知道的和你以为自己知道的之间的差距？

sentences.en: This week, on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周，锁定《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Human beings are, as far as we know, the most intelligent creatures ever produced by evolution.
sentences.zh: 就我们所知，人类是进化产物中最聪明的生物。

sentences.en: Our brains are unimaginably complex and capable of extraordinary feats of invention and creativity.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑复杂得难以想象，能够完成非凡的发明和创造壮举。

sentences.en: And yet, these amazing minds also come with certain limits.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些神奇的大脑也伴随着某些局限性。

sentences.en: At the University of Colorado Boulder, Philip Fernbeck is a cognitive scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 在科罗拉多大学博尔德分校，菲利普·费恩贝克是一位认知科学家。

sentences.en: He has spent many years studying a rather humbling question.
sentences.zh: 他多年来一直在研究一个相当考验人的问题。

sentences.en: How much do we actually know about the world in which we live?
sentences.zh: 我们对我们所生活的世界到底了解多少？

sentences.en: Phil Fernbeck, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 菲尔·费恩贝克，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: It's great to be with you, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起，香卡。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Phil, in 1946, eight men gathered in a nuclear lab in Los Alamos, New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 菲尔，1946年，八名男子聚集在新墨西哥州洛斯阿拉莫斯的一个核实验室里。

sentences.en: They were there to watch a distinguished researcher perform a maneuver known as Tickling the Dragon's Tail.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里观看一位杰出的研究员执行一项被称为“逗弄恶龙尾巴”的操作。

sentences.en: Who were these people, Phil?
sentences.zh: 这些人是谁，菲尔？

sentences.en: What was going on?
sentences.zh: 当时发生了什么？

sentences.en: This was one of the most fascinating periods in American history.
sentences.zh: 这是美国历史上最迷人的时期之一。

sentences.en: It was the development of the nuclear bomb at Los Alamos in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 也就是在新墨西哥州洛斯阿拉莫斯研制原子弹的时期。

sentences.en: And these were very eminent physicists who were testing the reaction of the fissile material in the bomb, the plutonium.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常杰出的物理学家，他们当时正在测试原子弹中可裂变材料（也就是钚）的反应。

sentences.en: And this particular experiment, which the physicist Richard Feynman, as you said, called Tickling the Dragon's Tail.
sentences.zh: 而这个特定的实验，正如你所说，被物理学家理查德·费曼称为“逗弄恶龙尾巴”。

sentences.en: It was a very delicate experiment that involved taking two hemispheres of beryllium that were surrounding the plutonium core
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常微妙的实验，涉及将包裹着钚核心的两半铍半球

sentences.en: and moving them closer and closer together to test the reactivity of the plutonium.
sentences.zh: 越推越近，以测试钚的反应活性。

sentences.en: So the plutonium is radioactive and gives off neutrons.
sentences.zh: 所以钚是放射性的，会释放中子。

sentences.en: Those neutrons rebound off of the beryllium and create the reaction.
sentences.zh: 这些中子从铍上反弹回来并产生反应。

sentences.en: As the hemispheres get closer together, you get more of that reaction.
sentences.zh: 随着两个半球靠得越近，你得到的这种反应就越多。

sentences.en: What's so delicate and dangerous about this experiment is that if the hemispheres get too close together,
sentences.zh: 这个实验之所以如此微妙和危险，是因为如果两个半球靠得太近，

sentences.en: it can create a chain reaction that releases a burst of radioactivity that can be very dangerous.
sentences.zh: 它会产生连锁反应，释放出一股非常危险的放射性辐射爆发。

sentences.en: So the lead scientist who was running this experiment, who was Tickling the Dragon's Tail, if you will,
sentences.zh: 所以负责这项实验的首席科学家，也就是可以说在“逗弄恶龙尾巴”的人，

sentences.en: was named Louis Slotin.
sentences.zh: 名叫路易斯·斯洛廷。

sentences.en: And he was a very experienced physicist, was he not?
sentences.zh: 他是一位经验非常丰富的物理学家，对吗？

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He was one of the developers of the bomb and was an extremely eminent and experienced physiciSt.
sentences.zh: 他是原子弹的研发者之一，是一位极其杰出且经验丰富的物理学家。

sentences.en: He was the most important member of this experimental team
sentences.zh: 他是这个实验团队中最重要的一员

sentences.en: because he was the one who was actually engaged in the process of bringing those hemispheres of beryllium closer together.
sentences.zh: 因为他是真正着手将那些铍半球拉近彼此的人。

sentences.en: How was he doing it?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: What was he doing?
sentences.zh: 他当时在做什么？

sentences.en: Well, this is the crazy part of the story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是这个故事疯狂的地方。

sentences.en: He was actually using a common flathead screwdriver to keep the two sections of beryllium apart.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是用一把普通的平头螺丝刀来隔开这两部分铍。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, at the critical moment, the screwdriver slipped.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在关键时刻，螺丝刀滑脱了。

sentences.en: The two hemispheres of beryllium crashed together and they released this intense burst of radioactive radiation.
sentences.zh: 两半铍半球猛烈撞击在一起，释放出了强烈放射性辐射的爆发。

sentences.en: Slotin, who was right next to the apparatus, took the worst of it.
sentences.zh: 斯洛廷就站在仪器旁边，承受了最严重的辐射。

sentences.en: And he actually died in the infirmary eight days later of radiation poisoning.
sentences.zh: 他实际上在八天后死于医务室的辐射中毒。

sentences.en: The rest of the physicists in the room, all eminent scientists, all survived the initial burSt.
sentences.zh: 房间里的其他物理学家，全都是杰出的科学家，都在最初的辐射爆发中幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Some of them, unfortunately, died before their time, potentially due to the radiation dose that they received.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，其中一些人过早离世，这可能与他们受到的辐射剂量有关。

sentences.en: Was there a way of conducting this experiment more safely?
sentences.zh: 有没有更安全地进行这项实验的方法？

sentences.en: There certainly was.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: For instance, an obvious way to do it would have been to suspend one of the hemispheres of beryllium
sentences.zh: 例如，一个显而易见的方法是将其中一个铍半球悬挂起来

sentences.en: and then the other hemisphere could be raised from the bottom.
sentences.zh: 然后另一个半球可以从底部向上升起。

sentences.en: In that case, if anything slipped or there was any problem, gravity would have just pulled the two hemispheres apart.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，如果有什么东西滑落或出现任何问题，重力就会把两个半球拉开。

sentences.en: And that would have been much less of a dangerous way to conduct the experiment.
sentences.zh: 那样进行实验的危险性会小得多。

sentences.en: Why do you think Lewis Slotin didn't do it that way, Phil?
sentences.zh: 你认为路易斯·斯洛廷为什么不那样做呢，菲尔？

sentences.en: I think Slotin, like any other person, by virtue of his experience, did not foresee this potential problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为斯洛廷和任何人一样，由于他的经验，没有预见到这个潜在的问题。

sentences.en: He became overconfident in his ability to conduct this experiment because he had done it so many times before
sentences.zh: 他对自己进行这项实验的能力变得过于自信，因为他以前做过很多次

sentences.en: and he had so much experience in this domain.
sentences.zh: 并且在这个领域拥有如此丰富的经验。

sentences.en: I want to ask you about another incident that took place many years later.
sentences.zh: 我想问你关于多年后发生的另一起事件。

sentences.en: In 2009, Air France Flight 447 crashed into the ocean, killing more than 200 passengers on board.
sentences.zh: 2009年，法航447航班坠入海洋，造成机上200多名乘客遇难。

sentences.en: When the black box of the plane was recovered, it appeared that the aircraft had stalled.
sentences.zh: 当飞机的黑匣子被找回时，情况表明飞机似乎失速了。

sentences.en: Can you first explain what a stall is and what you're supposed to do when the plane stalls
sentences.zh: 你能先解释一下什么是失速，以及飞机失速时你应该做什么

sentences.en: and what the pilots of Flight 447 actually did?
sentences.zh: 以及447航班的飞行员实际做了什么吗？

sentences.en: A stall is a very scary thing.
sentences.zh: 失速是一件非常可怕的事情。

sentences.en: So that's when an airplane loses airspeed and literally starts falling out of the sky.
sentences.zh: 也就是飞机失去空速并字面意义上开始从空中坠落的时候。

sentences.en: Every pilot, when they learn how to fly an airplane, this is one of the most important things that they train for.
sentences.zh: 每个飞行员在学习如何驾驶飞机时，这是他们训练的最重要的内容之一。

sentences.en: So they actually will purposely put the airplane into a stall and then learn how to take it out of the stall.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上会故意让飞机进入失速状态，然后学习如何使飞机脱离失速。

sentences.en: How do you take a plane out of a stall?
sentences.zh: 如何让飞机脱离失速？

sentences.en: Well, actually, what you need to do is point the nose of the plane down counterintuitively.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你需要做的是反直觉地把机头指向下方。

sentences.en: You want to go up, but you actually have to point the plane down.
sentences.zh: 你想往上飞，但你实际上必须把机头朝下。

sentences.en: You have to increase your acceleration.
sentences.zh: 你必须增加加速度。

sentences.en: You have to regain airspeed and then you can actually achieve an altitude correction.
sentences.zh: 你必须恢复空速，然后才能真正实现高度修正。

sentences.en: When they recovered the black box from this airplane, surprisingly,
sentences.zh: 当他们从这架飞机上找回黑匣子时，令人惊讶的是，

sentences.en: what they found was that this very experienced pilot had done was exactly the opposite of what you're supposed to do in a stall situation.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这位经验丰富的飞行员所做的，与你在失速情况下应该做的事情完全相反。

sentences.en: He was actually trying to pull the plane up, but without any airspeed, that's just impossible.
sentences.zh: 他实际上在试图把飞机拉起来，但在没有空速的情况下，这根本是不可能的。

sentences.en: There's no way that the plane could recover.
sentences.zh: 飞机绝无恢复的可能。

sentences.en: And so, unfortunately, this led to this devastating outcome.
sentences.zh: 所以，不幸的是，这导致了这个毁灭性的结果。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether the Federal Aviation Administration or other safety organizations evaluated why the error had come about.
sentences.zh: 我想知道美国联邦航空管理局或其他安全机构是否评估过这个错误是如何产生的。

sentences.en: Did they look into that, Phil?
sentences.zh: 他们调查过吗，菲尔？

sentences.en: Yeah, they did very extensive analyses to try to figure out what went wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们做了非常广泛的分析，试图弄清楚究竟哪里出了问题。

sentences.en: And one of their overall conclusions was that pilots in general have become too reliant on automation and have lost some of their basic flying skills.
sentences.zh: 他们的总体结论之一是，飞行员总体上变得过于依赖自动化，并丧失了一些基本飞行技能。

sentences.en: Modern airplanes, especially modern jetliners, are so technologically sophisticated that a lot of the time the software and the airplane are doing most of the work.
sentences.zh: 现代飞机，尤其是现代喷气式客机，在技术上如此先进，以至于很多时候软件和飞机都在做大部分工作。

sentences.en: The pilot is almost like an observer watching the airplane do the job.
sentences.zh: 飞行员几乎就像是一个观察员，看着飞机完成工作。

sentences.en: The pilot, of course, has to be there to intervene in unusual situations when something goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 当然，当发生问题时，飞行员必须在那里进行干预以应对异常情况。

sentences.en: The problem is that those situations are becoming more and more rare because the software is becoming more and more capable.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，由于软件变得越来越强大，这些情况正变得越来越少见。

sentences.en: So, in cases where an intervention is necessary, the pilot might not be as prepared as they should be because they become too reliant on the automation.
sentences.zh: 因此，在必须进行干预的情况下，飞行员可能无法做好应有的准备，因为他们过于依赖自动化。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm thinking in a much, much smaller scale, you know, I am so reliant on my, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想到了一个规模小得多的事情，你知道，我太依赖我的，你知道的，

sentences.en: navigation tools and GPS technology to get me around that on the occasions when my phone dies, I suddenly feel like I can't find my way out of a paper bag these days.
sentences.zh: 导航工具和GPS技术来带路，以至于每当我的手机没电时，如今我突然觉得自己连个纸袋子都走不出去了。

sentences.en: I've had the exact same experience.
sentences.zh: 我有过完全相同的经历。

sentences.en: In fact, I've heard stories of people driving into lakes because that's what the GPS tells them to do.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我听说过有人把车开进湖里的故事，因为GPS就是这么告诉他们的。

sentences.en: My own personal experience with this is I use self-driving software all the time when I'm driving now.
sentences.zh: 我个人对此的经历是，我现在开车时一直在使用自动驾驶软件。

sentences.en: It works remarkably well.
sentences.zh: 它运行得非常出色。

sentences.en: But one thing I've noticed over the last few years is that I've actually become a worse driver.
sentences.zh: 但过去几年我注意到的一件事是，我实际上变成了一个更糟糕的司机。

sentences.en: It's, you know, no one wants to admit to themselves that they've become a worse driver.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有人愿意承认自己变成了一个更糟糕的司机。

sentences.en: But for me, the evidence is kind of incontrovertible at this point because I've gotten into a few fender benders over the last few years, which I've never done before.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，证据在这一点上可以说是无可辩驳的，因为我在过去几年里遇到过几起轻微擦挂，而我以前从没这样过。

sentences.en: And so I've asked myself, what is going on here?
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在问自己，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And I really think it's because I've become so reliant on the car doing the work that I've lost my situational awareness.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为这是因为我太依赖汽车来完成工作，以至于我失去了态势感知能力。

sentences.en: And then when something unusual happens and I need to take over, I'm not ready to do it, just like a pilot on an automated airline.
sentences.zh: 然后，当发生异常情况我需要接管时，我还没准备好，就像自动化航空公司的飞行员一样。

sentences.en: Both the Los Alamos accident and the Air France crash involved highly experienced people who made seemingly elementary mistakes.
sentences.zh: 洛斯阿拉莫斯事故和法航坠机事件都涉及高度经验丰富的人，他们犯了看似初级的错误。

sentences.en: Phil's research suggests there are many other instances where less experienced people also make blunders,
sentences.zh: 菲尔的研究表明，还有许多其他情况下，经验较少的人也会犯下大错，

sentences.en: in part because they assume that other smart people know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为他们假设其他聪明人知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Take, for instance, the 2008 financial crash in the United States.
sentences.zh: 比如，2008年美国的金融危机。

sentences.en: The financial crash in 2008 was in a great part due to a massive decline in the value of these financial products,
sentences.zh: 2008年的金融危机很大程度上是因为这些金融产品价值的大幅下跌，

sentences.en: a certain kind of financial product called a derivative.
sentences.zh: 一种特定类型的金融产品叫做衍生品。

sentences.en: Derivatives are really complicated financial instruments.
sentences.zh: 衍生品是真的很复杂的金融工具。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to predict exactly how they're going to behave.
sentences.zh: 而且很难准确预测它们的表现会怎样。

sentences.en: Traders like derivatives because they can often generate really good returns.
sentences.zh: 交易员喜欢衍生品，因为它们通常能产生非常好的回报。

sentences.en: In financial markets, return is always correlated with risk.
sentences.zh: 在金融市场中，回报总是与风险相关的。

sentences.en: So if something has a high return, it's also going to have a high risk.
sentences.zh: 所以如果某样东西有高回报，它也必然会有高风险。

sentences.en: The problem with derivatives is because they're so complicated, it's often impossible to see the risk or it's very hard to see the risk.
sentences.zh: 衍生品的问题在于它们太复杂了，通常根本看不出风险，或者很难看出风险。

sentences.en: The risk only emerges in sort of unusual situations.
sentences.zh: 风险只会在某种不寻常的情况下出现。

sentences.en: So it's like the product is, you know, it seems to be behaving just very safely, but then something changes.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比这个产品，你知道的，它看起来表现得非常安全，但接着情况就变了。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, instead of losing 10% of its value, it loses 90% of its value or something like that.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，它非但没有损失10%的价值，反而损失了90%的价值，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Now, what ended up happening in the financial crisis was that these derivative products were ending up in places where they didn't belong,
sentences.zh: 结果在金融危机中发生的事情是，这些衍生品最终流向了不属于它们的地方，

sentences.en: in places that should not have been taking on this amount of risk.
sentences.zh: 流向了本不该承担如此巨额风险的地方。

sentences.en: Things like pension funds that should be relatively safe investments.
sentences.zh: 比如本该是相对安全投资的养老基金。

sentences.en: Why did they end up there?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们会流落到那里？

sentences.en: Because the people buying them just did not appreciate or realize how complicated they were.
sentences.zh: 因为购买它们的人根本没有意识到或搞懂它们有多复杂。

sentences.en: And so what happened was when the price of real estate in the United States started going down,
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，当美国的房地产价格开始下跌时，

sentences.en: these products, which were tied to the value of real estate and like the default probabilities on mortgages,
sentences.zh: 这些与房地产价值以及按揭贷款违约概率等挂钩的产品，

sentences.en: they crashed in value.
sentences.zh: 它们的价值崩盘了。

sentences.en: And there was this huge amount of risk in our financial system because these products had entered into all these different areas
sentences.zh: 我们的金融系统里因此积聚了巨额风险，因为这些产品已经渗透到所有这些不同的领域，

sentences.en: and they were highly represented in all these different areas.
sentences.zh: 并且在所有这些不同的领域中占比很高。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, kind of everybody was caught by surprise that, you know,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，可以说是每个人都始料未及，

sentences.en: the pension fund was losing a huge amount of its value because it had exposure to these very risky things
sentences.zh: 养老基金损失了其巨额价值，因为它暴露在这些高风险事物之中，

sentences.en: because people didn't realize that the risk was there.
sentences.zh: 而人们却没有意识到风险就在那里。

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, it's analogous to what happened on the plane.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些方面，这类似于飞机上发生的事情。

sentences.en: You know, the planes are getting so complex that the pilots, in fact, are trusting the plane most of the time to fly itself.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，飞机变得越来越复杂，以至于飞行员在大多数时间里实际上都在信任飞机自己飞行。

sentences.en: And perhaps traders or people who manage pension funds are basically looking out at the market
sentences.zh: 也许交易员或养老基金管理者基本上也是在观察市场，

sentences.en: and the market has gotten so complex that they basically are saying, OK, we trust that these big banks know what they're doing,
sentences.zh: 而市场变得如此复杂，以至于他们基本上在说，好吧，我们相信这些大银行知道自己在做什么，

sentences.en: these big hedge funds know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 这些大型对冲基金知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And in some ways, they're outsourcing or reducing their own capabilities to actually deal with a crisis,
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，他们把应对危机的自身能力外包或削弱了，

sentences.en: partly because the situation has gotten so complex.
sentences.zh: 部分原因正是因为局势变得太复杂了。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think it happens at more than one level.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这种情况发生在不止一个层面。

sentences.en: So if you think about a pension fund manager who knows what a derivative is but isn't a super expert in a derivative,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想想一个养老基金经理，他知道什么是衍生品，但并不是衍生品的超级专家，

sentences.en: he's relying on the people who do the analysis of the derivatives to kind of think,
sentences.zh: 他就会依赖那些对衍生品进行分析的人来思考，

sentences.en: oh, this is potentially like a good investment vehicle for my portfolio.
sentences.zh: 哦，这对我的投资组合来说可能是一个很好的投资工具。

sentences.en: He's not thinking in super careful detail about what the risk profile is of that instrument.
sentences.zh: 他并没有超级仔细地去考虑该金融工具的风险状况是什么样的。

sentences.en: And maybe he or she should be, but they obviously didn't.
sentences.zh: 也许他或她本该如此，但很明显他们并没有这样做。

sentences.en: But it also occurs at another level, which is the person who actually is the super expert on the derivative,
sentences.zh: 但它也发生在另一个层面，那就是真正精通衍生品的超级专家，

sentences.en: even that person, it turned out, didn't understand completely how these things were going to behave.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，连这样的人也并没有完全理解这些东西将如何表现。

sentences.en: So the big banks who were developing these instruments and selling them,
sentences.zh: 因此，那些开发并销售这些金融工具的大银行，

sentences.en: they would have a mathematical model that would determine exactly how these things would behave.
sentences.zh: 他们会有一个数学模型来精确决定这些东西将如何表现。

sentences.en: The problem is that those mathematical models work really well most of the time,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，这些数学模型在大多数时候运行得非常好，

sentences.en: like an airplane that's highly automated, but they actually break down in very unusual situations.
sentences.zh: 就像一架高度自动化的飞机，但它们在非常不寻常的情况下确实会崩溃。

sentences.en: A black swan event, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 可以说是黑天鹅事件。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what happened.
sentences.zh: 而这正是发生的事情。

sentences.en: So the models failed.
sentences.zh: 所以模型失效了。

sentences.en: And so the super experts on derivatives,
sentences.zh: 因此，那些衍生品超级专家，

sentences.en: even they completely misunderstood the amount of risk that was present in these products.
sentences.zh: 连他们也完全误解了这些产品中存在的风险程度。

sentences.en: So it was across the entire financial system that there was these sort of miscalibrations in understanding.
sentences.zh: 因此，整个金融系统都充斥着这种理解上的校准偏差。

sentences.en: And there was this cascade effect that started with some slight decreases in the price of housing
sentences.zh: 并且产生了一种级联效应，从房价的小幅下跌开始，

sentences.en: and then just cascaded into this massive crash and devastation that not only affected the United States,
sentences.zh: 然后级联引发了巨大的崩盘和破坏，不仅影响了美国，

sentences.en: but affected countries all over the world because the entire global system is so connected nowadays.
sentences.zh: 还影响了世界各地的国家，因为如今整个全球系统是如此紧密相连。

sentences.en: When we come back, why we imagine we know more than we do and what we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨为什么我们自以为懂得比实际更多，以及我们能对此做些什么。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Perhaps you've had the experience of driving to an important event.
sentences.zh: 也许你有过这样的经历：开车去参加一个重要活动。

sentences.en: You're running late and you decide you want to outsmart all the other drivers who are stuck in traffic.
sentences.zh: 你快迟到了，决定要智胜其他所有堵在路上的司机。

sentences.en: You take a side street because you know it's a shortcut around the traffic jam.
sentences.zh: 你走了一条小路，因为你知道那是绕过交通拥堵的捷径。

sentences.en: Three blocks later, you realize the shortcut isn't a shortcut.
sentences.zh: 三个街区后，你意识到这条捷径根本不是捷径。

sentences.en: In fact, it doesn't get you where you need to go.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它根本带不到你想去的地方。

sentences.en: What do you tell yourself in moments like that?
sentences.zh: 在这样的时刻，你对自己说些什么？

sentences.en: Do you say, oh, I got that really wrong?
sentences.zh: 你会说，哦，我真的错得离谱吗？

sentences.en: Or do you say, my sense of navigation is impeccable, except for this one tiny misstep?
sentences.zh: 还是会说，我的方向感无可挑剔，除了这一个小小的失误？

sentences.en: Philip Fernback is a cognitive scientist at the Leeds School of Business at the University of Colorado Boulder.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·费恩巴克是科罗拉多大学博尔德分校利兹商学院的一名认知科学家。

sentences.en: Phil, as a cognitive scientist, you've studied how humans can be so brilliant, but also really dumb.
sentences.zh: 菲尔，作为一名认知科学家，你研究过人类怎么能如此聪明，但有时又真的很蠢。

sentences.en: That feels like a paradox.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是一个悖论。

sentences.en: That is a paradox, and that is the paradox at the heart of humankind, I think.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个悖论，我认为这也是人类心灵核心处的悖论。

sentences.en: On the one hand, we have visited the moon and created incredible artificial intelligence and all these other sort of almost magical abilities.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我们已经造访过月球，创造了不可思议的人工智能以及所有这些其他近乎神奇的能力。

sentences.en: On the other hand, everybody knows that people can engage in behavior that's incredibly ignorant and extreme and foolish.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，大家都知道人们会做出极其无知、极端和愚蠢的行为。

sentences.en: And we've all done it ourselves, and we've all seen it in others.
sentences.zh: 我们自己都做过，也都曾在别人身上看到过。

sentences.en: So researchers who study the mind have come up with a term to describe why our own ignorance is often hidden from us.
sentences.zh: 因此，研究人类思维的研究人员想出了一个术语，来描述为什么我们自己的无知常常对我们隐瞒起来。

sentences.en: They call it the illusion of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为知识的错觉。

sentences.en: What is this illusion, Phil?
sentences.zh: 菲尔，什么是这种错觉？

sentences.en: The illusion of knowledge is the idea that we think that we understand the world in much greater detail than we actually do.
sentences.zh: 知识的错觉是指这样一种观点：我们认为自己对世界的理解比实际情况要详细得多。

sentences.en: In cognitive science, this is sometimes called the illusion of explanatory depth.
sentences.zh: 在认知科学中，这有时被称为解释深度的错觉。

sentences.en: There was great research done by a psychologist at Yale named Frank Kyle and his colleagues in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 耶鲁大学的一位心理学家弗兰克·凯尔和他的同事们在20世纪90年代做过一项伟大的研究。

sentences.en: And that's precisely what they were interested in.
sentences.zh: 这正是他们感兴趣的课题。

sentences.en: How well do people understand how everyday objects work?
sentences.zh: 人们对日常用品的工作原理理解得有多好？

sentences.en: Things like toilets or ballpoint pens or zippers.
sentences.zh: 比如马桶、圆珠笔或拉链。

sentences.en: And in these studies, what they asked people to do was to first just give a sort of impression of how well they understand things.
sentences.zh: 在这些研究中，他们要求人们做的第一件事就是大致给出一个印象：他们觉得自己对事物的理解有多深。

sentences.en: And what's fun about this experiment is that your listeners can actually do this experiment on themselves right now.
sentences.zh: 这个实验有趣的地方在于，你的听众现在就可以在自己身上做这个实验。

sentences.en: So think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以想想看。

sentences.en: How well do you understand how a toilet works?
sentences.zh: 你对马桶的工作原理理解得有多好？

sentences.en: And if you're like most people, you're kind of nodding your head right now and saying, well, I have a decent understanding of how a toilet works.
sentences.zh: 如果你和大多数人一样，你现在可能正点着头说，嗯，我对马桶的工作原理有相当不错的理解。

sentences.en: You think that somewhere in your mind is something like an annotated plumbing diagram that you could tell us about.
sentences.zh: 你认为你的脑海深处有什么类似带注释的管道图纸的东西，你可以给我们详细讲讲。

sentences.en: But here's the trick.
sentences.zh: 但诀窍来了。

sentences.en: In the next part of the experiment, what I'm going to do is I'm going to ask you to explain to me in detail exactly how it works.
sentences.zh: 在实验的下一部分，我要做的是，我将要求你向我详细解释它到底是怎样工作的。

sentences.en: And when I do that, something really remarkable happens.
sentences.zh: 当我这么做时，一件非常奇妙的事情发生了。

sentences.en: People reach inside and they realize they have just about nothing to say.
sentences.zh: 人们内省时会发现自己几乎无话可说。

sentences.en: It turns out that we tend to know remarkably little about the way that the world works.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我们对世界运转方式的了解少得惊人。

sentences.en: And yet that initial impression we have is that we do understand in a lot of depth.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们最初的印象却是我们理解得很深。

sentences.en: And that's what Kyle called the illusion of explanatory depth and is sometimes referred to more simply as an illusion of knowledge or an illusion of understanding.
sentences.zh: 这就是凯尔所说的解释深度的错觉，有时更简单地被称为知识的错觉或理解的错觉。

sentences.en: So when it comes to something like a toilet, I think most people imagine, you know, you press a handle and water flows into the bowl and the toilet flushes.
sentences.zh: 所以当谈到像马桶这样的东西时，我想大多数人都会想象，你知道的，你按下把手，水流入水箱，马桶就冲水了。

sentences.en: And that's how the toilet works.
sentences.zh: 马桶就是这样工作的。

sentences.en: So that's actually, most of the time, pretty much all you need to know about how a toilet works until the toilet breaks and you have to fix it.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，在大多数情况下，关于马桶是如何工作的，你只需要知道这么多，直到马桶坏了你得去修它。

sentences.en: And then you realize, actually, there's a lot more going on.
sentences.zh: 然后你才会意识到，实际上里面还有很多门道。

sentences.en: At this point, you may be asking yourself, how do toilets work?
sentences.zh: 此时，你可能会问自己：马桶到底是怎样工作的？

sentences.en: I asked Phil to test his own knowledge, but he declined to offer an explanation from memory.
sentences.zh: 我让菲尔测试他自己的知识，但他拒绝凭记忆做出解释。

sentences.en: As he put it, he's learned it about 10 million times, but can never retain it.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，他已经学过大约一千万次了，但从来记不住。

sentences.en: So here he is, reading the explanation.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，他正在朗读解释。

sentences.en: So the most popular flush toilet in North America is the siphoning toilet.
sentences.zh: 那么，北美最流行的抽水马桶是虹吸式马桶。

sentences.en: And by the way, this is a really ingenious mechanism that was created.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这是一个非常巧妙的机制。

sentences.en: Its most important components are a tank, a bowl, and a trapway.
sentences.zh: 它最重要的组件是水箱、马桶盆和存水弯。

sentences.en: The trapway is usually S or U-shaped, and it curves up higher than the outlet of the bowl before descending into the drainpipe that eventually feeds the sewer.
sentences.zh: 存水弯通常呈S形或U形，它的曲线向上高于马桶盆的出口，然后下降进入最终通往排污管道的排水管。

sentences.en: The tank is initially full of water.
sentences.zh: 水箱最初是装满水的。

sentences.en: And when the toilet is flushed, the water flows from the tank quickly into the bowl, raising the water level above the highest curve of the trapway.
sentences.zh: 当马桶冲水时，水从水箱快速流入马桶盆，使水位上升超过存水弯的最高曲线。

sentences.en: This purges the trapway of air, filling it with water.
sentences.zh: 这会排出存水弯中的空气，使其充满水。

sentences.en: As soon as the trapway fills, the magic occurs.
sentences.zh: 一旦存水弯充满水，奇迹就发生了。

sentences.en: A siphon effect is created that sucks the water out of the bowl and sends it through the trapway down the drain.
sentences.zh: 就会产生一种虹吸效应，把马桶盆里的水吸出来，并通过存水弯送入排水管。

sentences.en: It's the same siphon action that you can use to steal gasoline out of a car by placing one end in the tank and sucking on the other end.
sentences.zh: 这和你可以用来从汽车里偷汽油的虹吸原理是一样的，只要把一端放进油箱，然后吮吸另一端。

sentences.en: Let me try and say it back to you to see if I can test my own illusion of knowledge here.
sentences.zh: 让我试着向你复述一遍，看看我能否在这里测试一下我自己的知识错觉。

sentences.en: What I think it's saying is that you have this S-shaped curve in the pipe behind the toilet bowl.
sentences.zh: 我认为它的意思是，马桶盆后方的管道里有一个S形的弯管。

sentences.en: And as you flush the toilet, it fills with water.
sentences.zh: 当你冲马桶时，它会充满水。

sentences.en: It starts to fill up this S-shaped pipe.
sentences.zh: 它开始填满这个S形管道。

sentences.en: And as it fills up the pipe with water, the water basically pushes out the air, creating something of a vacuum on the back end of this S-shaped pipe.
sentences.zh: 随着水充满管道，水基本上把空气挤了出去，在这个S形管道的后端产生了一点真空。

sentences.en: And the vacuum then suctions the rest of the water inside the bowl out into the drain.
sentences.zh: 然后这个真空就会把马桶盆里剩下的水吸到排水管里。

sentences.en: How did I do, Phil?
sentences.zh: 菲尔，我表现得怎么样？

sentences.en: Well, I think we should test that with a plumber, not with me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我们应该找个水管工来测试，而不是找我。

sentences.en: But I think you did a pretty good job.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你做得相当不错。

sentences.en: What you're saying is I should stick to podcasting and not plumbing is the advice I'm hearing you give me.
sentences.zh: 我听到你给我的建议是，我应该坚持做播客，而不是去修水管。

sentences.en: I think we both should.
sentences.zh: 我想我们俩都应该这样。

sentences.en: But what this highlights is just how complicated the world is.
sentences.zh: 但这也凸显了世界是多么复杂。

sentences.en: Whoever thought, you know, there's this ingenious mechanism in this object that we use every single day and we never think about.
sentences.zh: 谁会想到，你知道的，在我们每天都在使用却从不思考的这个物体里，竟然有这样巧妙的机制。

sentences.en: So talk a moment about how the illusion of knowledge in some ways is a product of the way the human mind works and its limitations as it interacts with this extremely complex world.
sentences.zh: 所以请谈谈为什么知识的错觉在某些方面是人类思维运作方式的产物，以及它在与这个极其复杂的社会交互时的局限性。

sentences.en: Why is it that the workings of the world are so hard for us to wrap our heads around, Phil?
sentences.zh: 菲尔，为什么世界的运作方式让我们如此难以理解？

sentences.en: I think this reflects a really deep fact about the nature of the mind and what thinking is actually for.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了关于人类思维本质以及思考真正用途的一个极其深刻的事实。

sentences.en: Thinking evolved to make us more effective at acting in the world.
sentences.zh: 思考的进化是为了让我们在世间行事时更加有效。

sentences.en: The world is extremely complex.
sentences.zh: 世界极其复杂。

sentences.en: And to be able to choose effective actions in the world really requires acting in environments that are very different from one another.
sentences.zh: 为了能够在世界上选择有效的行动，确实需要在截然不同的环境中采取行动。

sentences.en: We almost never see the same exact situation arise twice.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎从来没有看到过完全相同的情况发生两次。

sentences.en: And so our minds have to be really effective at generalization.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的思维必须非常擅长归纳。

sentences.en: They have to understand that this situation is similar to this situation in some way to be able to act effectively.
sentences.zh: 为了能够有效地采取行动，它们必须理解这种情况在某种程度上类似于那种情况。

sentences.en: So storing a huge amount of detail about the world and the way that it works is actually counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 因此，存储关于世界及其运作方式的大量细节实际上是适得其反的。

sentences.en: What we really want to do is throw away all of the irrelevant detail and just retain the deeper principles,
sentences.zh: 我们真正想做的是抛弃所有无关的细节，只保留更深层的原则，

sentences.en: the deeper generalizable structures that are going to allow us to choose effective actions.
sentences.zh: 即那些能让我们选择有效行动的更深层的可归纳结构。

sentences.en: And of course, this must be true for all manner of different things in the world, everything from bacteria to how trees work to how a hurricane works.
sentences.zh: 当然，世界上各种各样的事情一定都是如此，从细菌到树木的工作原理，再到飓风的工作原理。

sentences.en: All of these in some ways are complex phenomena where we have a general understanding of what bacteria do, a general understanding of what a hurricane is,
sentences.zh: 所有这些在某些方面都是复杂的现象，我们对细菌的作用有大致的了解，对什么是飓风有大致的了解，

sentences.en: but not the exact mechanics of what's actually happening at a granular level.
sentences.zh: 但却没有在颗粒度层面上实际发生的事情的精确力学原理。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The world is so complex when you start when you start digging into the details of almost anything,
sentences.zh: 当你开始深入了解几乎任何事物的细节时，你会发现世界是如此复杂，

sentences.en: you realize how complicated it is and that you don't necessarily appreciate that complexity off the bat.
sentences.zh: 你会意识到它的复杂程度，并且你一开始未必能体会到这种复杂性。

sentences.en: I remember hearing a story about a rock, paper, scissors tournament.
sentences.zh: 我记得听过一个关于石头、剪刀、布锦标赛的故事。

sentences.en: Do you know the game rock, paper, scissors?
sentences.zh: 你知道石头、剪刀、布这个游戏吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Very simple game, right?
sentences.zh: 非常简单的游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: It seems like there's nothing to learn and nothing to understand about that game.
sentences.zh: 这个游戏似乎没什么可学的，也没什么可理解的。

sentences.en: How could you have a tournament?
sentences.zh: 怎么可能举办锦标赛？

sentences.en: You just throw randomly.
sentences.zh: 你随便出就行了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, actually, it turns out that there's a group of people who have gotten really good at rock, paper, scissors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，结果证明有一群人已经把石头、剪刀、布玩得很精通了。

sentences.en: And what do they do?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做的？

sentences.en: They master the details of how the human mind chooses what to throw and how it engages in pattern matching and other kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他们掌握了人类心理如何选择出拳、如何进行模式匹配以及其他各种行为的细节。

sentences.en: And they can identify certain kinds of patterns in what a more novice rock, paper, scissors player will do and take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 他们可以识别出较不成熟的石头、剪刀、布玩家所做出的某些模式，并利用这一点。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: So, in other words, if I'm a novice, there might be certain patterns that I slip into unconsciously without realizing I've slipped into the pattern.
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，如果我是一个新手，可能会在不知不觉中陷入某些模式，而自己却没有意识到。

sentences.en: And if you're an expert, you sort of can take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 而如果你是一个专家，你就可以某种程度上利用这一点。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It's a funny kind of dumb example, but something where when I first looked at it, I said, there is no way that somebody could develop any level of expertise in that area.
sentences.zh: 这是一个挺有意思的笨例子，当我第一次看到它时，我说，绝对不可能有人能在那个领域达到任何程度的专业水平。

sentences.en: But it turns out, no, there is actually something to be learned there.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，并非如此，那里确实有些东西可以学。

sentences.en: So, we can see the problem with mastering too much detail about the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可以看到掌握过多世界细节所带来的问题。

sentences.en: When we look at people with a very rare condition called hyperthymesia, what is this condition, Phil?
sentences.zh: 当我们观察患有一种名为超忆症的罕见疾病的人时，菲尔，这是一种什么病？

sentences.en: How does it work?
sentences.zh: 它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a super fascinating example.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个超级吸引人的例子。

sentences.en: So, hyperthymesia is also called highly superior autobiographical memory.
sentences.zh: 超忆症也被称为高度优越的自传体记忆。

sentences.en: And these are people who literally remember everything that's ever happened to them.
sentences.zh: 这些人字面意思上能记住发生在他们身上的所有事情。

sentences.en: And so, you could talk to a person with hyperthymesia and say, what happened to you at 1030 in the morning on August 15th, 1985?
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以和一个患有超忆症的人交谈，然后问：1985年8月15日早上10点30分，你发生了什么事？

sentences.en: And they can relate to exactly what occurred.
sentences.zh: 他们就能说出当时究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: They basically have perfect recall.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上拥有完美的记忆力。

sentences.en: So, before I described how our minds are very good at throwing away irrelevant detail.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我刚才所说，我们的大脑非常擅长抛弃不相关的细节。

sentences.en: If you have hyperthymesia, it's the opposite.
sentences.zh: 如果你有超忆症，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: You retain everything that's ever happened to you.
sentences.zh: 你会保留所有发生在你身上的事情。

sentences.en: But it sounds like a superpower, but it actually makes life really difficult.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是一个超能力，但实际上却让生活变得非常艰难。

sentences.en: And there's an amazing short story by the Argentinian writer Borges, which is called Funes the Memorius.
sentences.zh: 阿根廷作家博尔赫斯写过一篇精彩的短篇小说，叫做《博闻强记的富内斯》。

sentences.en: And it describes exactly this, a man who falls off a horse and develops perfect autobiographical memory
sentences.zh: 它准确地描述了这一点：一个从马上摔下来并发展出完美自传体记忆的男人，

sentences.en: so that he remembers every little detail of his life.
sentences.zh: 他能记住生活中的每一个微小细节。

sentences.en: And it drives him crazy.
sentences.zh: 这把他逼疯了。

sentences.en: And that's because the purpose of thinking, the purpose of cognition, is really not to store detail.
sentences.zh: 这是因为思考的目的、认知的目的，其实并不是为了储存细节。

sentences.en: It's to throw the detail away to be able to generalize.
sentences.zh: 而是为了抛弃细节，从而能够进行概括。

sentences.en: And that's such an important function of cognition.
sentences.zh: 这是认知的一个非常重要的功能。

sentences.en: If you have this hyperthymesia, it actually makes life really difficult.
sentences.zh: 如果你有这种超忆症，它实际上会使生活变得非常艰难。

sentences.en: So, what I hear you saying, Phil, is that in many ways, it's actually more efficient and more effective for us to discard a lot of details,
sentences.zh: 菲尔，我听你的意思，在许多方面，丢弃大量细节对我们来说实际上更有效率、也更有效，

sentences.en: or maybe even never learn the details in the first place, and stick with this very generalized, you know, understanding of the world.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至一开始就不要去学这些细节，而是坚持这种非常广义的、你知道的对世界的理解。

sentences.en: So, the problem is not that we don't know everything.
sentences.zh: 所以，问题不在于我们不知道所有事情。

sentences.en: That's just the human condition.
sentences.zh: 这就是人类的现状。

sentences.en: The problem is that most of us think we know more than we actually do.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们大多数人都觉得自己知道的比实际知道的要多。

sentences.en: In fact, it would be futile to try to know everything.
sentences.zh: 事实上，试图了解一切将是徒劳的。

sentences.en: The world is just way too complex.
sentences.zh: 世界实在是太复杂了。

sentences.en: We've already talked about that.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论过这一点了。

sentences.en: There's just no way that an individual can know enough about the world that it would be effective to store all the details about everything.
sentences.zh: 个人根本没有办法对世界有足够的了解，从而把关于一切的细节全部储存起来还能保持高效。

sentences.en: That's just part and parcel of what it means to be a human being.
sentences.zh: 这正是身为人类所固有的一部分。

sentences.en: It is a problem that we don't appreciate the extent to which we don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我们没有意识到自己不理解的程度，这本身就是一个问题。

sentences.en: So, in April 1995, a man named MacArthur Wheeler came up with what seemed to him to be a foolproof way to rob banks and get away with it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1995年4月，一个名叫麦克阿瑟·惠勒的人想出了他认为万无一失的方法来抢劫银行并逃脱法网。

sentences.en: Tell me what he did, Phil.
sentences.zh: 告诉我他是怎么做的，菲尔。

sentences.en: This is a crazy story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个疯狂的故事。

sentences.en: So, this guy was under the impression that he would be invisible to the cameras if he put lemon juice on his face.
sentences.zh: 这个家伙深信不疑，如果他在脸上涂上柠檬汁，摄像头就拍不到他了。

sentences.en: You remember when you were a kid, you could create invisible ink by putting lemon juice on the paper.
sentences.zh: 你还记得小时候，你可以用柠檬汁在纸上写隐形字吗？

sentences.en: So, he thought for some reason that this would apply to making him invisible to the camera.
sentences.zh: 所以他出于某种原因认为，这同样适用于让自己在摄像头前隐身。

sentences.en: So, he actually went in to try to rob a bank with no mask, no subterfuse whatsoever, just lemon juice on his face.
sentences.zh: 于是他真的没有戴面具、没有任何伪装，就走进去试图抢劫银行，脸上只涂了柠檬汁。

sentences.en: So, his image is broadcast on the news.
sentences.zh: 所以他的形象在新闻上播出了。

sentences.en: Within minutes, the police arrive at his door to arrest him, and he is completely incredulous.
sentences.zh: 几分钟之内，警察就来到他家门口逮捕了他，而他感到完全不可置信。

sentences.en: How could they have possibly known it was him?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么可能知道是他？

sentences.en: Because he had the lemon juice on his face.
sentences.zh: 就因为他脸上涂了柠檬汁。

sentences.en: And, in fact, it turned out that he had tested the method by taking a Polaroid of himself
sentences.zh: 事实上，事实证明他测试过这个方法，方法是给自己拍了一张宝丽来照片，

sentences.en: and making sure that his face was indeed invisible to the Polaroid camera.
sentences.zh: 并确保他的脸在宝丽来相机里确实是隐形的。

sentences.en: It's never been discovered why the Polaroid didn't show his face.
sentences.zh: 人们一直没有发现为什么宝丽来没有拍到他的脸。

sentences.en: But, one possibility is that he missed because his eyes were filled with lemon juice.
sentences.zh: 但有一种可能是他没对准，因为他的眼睛里充满了柠檬汁。

sentences.en: So, what you're saying is he was not just a terrible bank robber, he was a terrible photographer as well.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，他不仅是个糟糕的银行劫匪，还是个糟糕的摄影师。

sentences.en: Apparently so.
sentences.zh: 显然是的。

sentences.en: Phil has also found that our faulty memories play a role in the illusion of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 菲尔还发现，我们有缺陷的记忆在知识错觉中发挥了作用。

sentences.en: Take, for instance, the research into how good people think they are when it comes to making smart investments in the stock market.
sentences.zh: 以研究为例，人们在股市中进行明智投资时，认为自己有多优秀。

sentences.en: It's been well documented that people tend to be very overconfident in their capabilities in terms of beating the market.
sentences.zh: 有充分的文献证明，人们往往对自己在战胜市场方面的能力过于自信。

sentences.en: And that can lead to really disastrous outcomes, like people take on too much risk.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致灾难性的结果，比如人们承担了过多的风险。

sentences.en: And it actually turns out that the more people actively trade, the worse they do.
sentences.zh: 事实上，事实证明，人们交易越活跃，他们的表现就越糟糕。

sentences.en: And active trading is sort of an indicator of being overconfident in your ability to beat the market.
sentences.zh: 而频繁交易可以说是对你战胜市场能力过度自信的一个指标。

sentences.en: This is a paper that I wrote with Dan Walters.
sentences.zh: 这是我和丹·沃尔特斯合写的一篇论文。

sentences.en: And what we found in this paper is that one reason for the overconfidence,
sentences.zh: 我们在论文中发现，过度自信的一个原因，

sentences.en: the reason that people feel that they can beat the market,
sentences.zh: 人们觉得自己能战胜市场的原因，

sentences.en: is because they tend to remember the good outcomes and forget the bad outcomes.
sentences.zh: 是因为他们往往记得好的结果，而忘记坏的结果。

sentences.en: So if I make a trade and I do great on it, that one's going to stick in my memory.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我做了一笔交易并且干得漂亮，那一笔就会留在我的记忆中。

sentences.en: More so than when I make a trade and it does poorly.
sentences.zh: 比起我做了一笔表现不佳的交易，记忆更深刻。

sentences.en: That's not to say that if you have a really disastrous trade, that you're not going to remember that.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说如果你有一笔非常灾难性的交易，你就不会记得它。

sentences.en: You certainly would.
sentences.zh: 你当然会记得。

sentences.en: But on average, you're going to tend to inflate the good over the bad.
sentences.zh: 但平均而言，你往往会夸大好的结果，而忽视坏的结果。

sentences.en: And one reason for that is because we tend to remember the things that help us maintain a positive self-image.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因是，我们倾向于记住那些有助于我们维持积极自我形象的事情。

sentences.en: We want to believe that we're smart and good at investing.
sentences.zh: 我们希望相信自己聪明并且擅长投资。

sentences.en: And that's a very natural human tendency to want to remember the good and kind of forget the bad.
sentences.zh: 想要记住美好事物并忘掉糟糕事物的愿望，是非常自然的人类倾向。

sentences.en: And so this doesn't just occur in the domain of investing, but can occur in other domains as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅发生在投资领域，也可能发生在其他领域。

sentences.en: So we've looked at how the illusion of knowledge and the illusion of explanatory depth,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们已经探讨了知识错觉和解释深度的错觉，

sentences.en: you know, applies to physical objects, things like bicycles or toilets.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如何适用于物理对象，比如自行车或马桶。

sentences.en: Can they also apply to historical events or public policy in that we imagine that we understand things better than we actually do, Phil?
sentences.zh: 它们是否也适用于历史事件或公共政策，即我们想象自己对事物的理解比实际情况更好，菲尔？

sentences.en: Um, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: And that is what made me so passionate about these ideas, um,
sentences.zh: 这就是让我对这些观点如此热衷的原因，嗯，

sentences.en: because it turns out that the reason that we should care about this illusion is not because people don't understand how a ballpoint pen or a toilet works.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，我们应该关注这种错觉的原因，并不是因为人们不明白圆珠笔或马桶是如何工作的。

sentences.en: But I realized at some point that the illusion applies to just about everything that we grapple with as a society and as individuals.
sentences.zh: 但我后来意识到，这种错觉几乎适用于我们作为社会和个人所面对的一切事物。

sentences.en: Um, I was doing this work in the midst of a political environment in the United States that was becoming more and more polarized.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我做这项工作时正值美国的政治环境变得越来越极化。

sentences.en: Um, and as I was doing this work, I had this, this big insight that, wow, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在做这项工作时，我有了这个重大的洞察，哇，嗯，

sentences.en: we are arguing with incredible vitriol across the aisle about issues that are extremely complex and that nobody understands in a lot of depth and detail.
sentences.zh: 我们在跨越党派时，带着令人难以置信的尖刻言辞进行争论，争论的问题极其复杂，而且没有人有很深的深度和细节理解。

sentences.en: And yet we have these passionate, strong views and, um, are unable to compromise, um, across the political divide.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们有着充满激情的强烈观点，而且，嗯，无法跨越政治鸿沟进行妥协，嗯。

sentences.en: And that was a core issue that really got me interested in this stuff.
sentences.zh: 这是让我真正对这些东西产生兴趣的核心问题。

sentences.en: Now, I think if you talk to a lot of people with strong political opinions, they will say, well, you know, I do understand the issues.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想如果你和许多有强烈政治观点的人交谈，他们会说，嗯，你知道，我确实理解这些问题。

sentences.en: I do understand what it means to have, you know, universal health care.
sentences.zh: 我确实理解拥有全民医疗意味着什么。

sentences.en: I do understand the consequences of a flat tax.
sentences.zh: 我确实理解单一税的后果。

sentences.en: Are they wrong?
sentences.zh: 他们错了吗？

sentences.en: I think in many cases they are wrong.
sentences.zh: 我认为在许多情况下他们是错的。

sentences.en: And actually we've demonstrated that in experiments.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们已经在实验中证明了这一点。

sentences.en: So, um, what we've done is something very akin to the toilet experiment that I described earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我们所做的事情非常类似于我之前描述的马桶实验。

sentences.en: We bring people into the lab and we ask them about their position on the issues of the day, the things that we're arguing about as a society.
sentences.zh: 我们把人们请进实验室，询问他们对当前热门问题的立场，也就是我们在社会上争论的事情。

sentences.en: And then we ask them how well they understand those issues.
sentences.zh: 然后我们询问他们对这些问题的理解程度。

sentences.en: People tend to say, oh yeah, I understand it pretty well.
sentences.zh: 人们往往会说，哦，是的，我相当理解。

sentences.en: And then we ask them to explain the mechanism, explain in detail how it works.
sentences.zh: 然后我们要求他们解释其机制，详细解释它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Um, and we find this large decrease in the sense of understanding.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们发现理解感大幅下降。

sentences.en: So people are humbled by that because they try to explain and they realize, wow, I just have a talking point or two.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们对此感到谦卑，因为他们试图解释，然后意识到，哇，我只有一个或两个谈资。

sentences.en: I actually don't understand this thing in detail.
sentences.zh: 我实际上并不详细了解这东西。

sentences.en: You've also found that people who have some of the strongest views on an issue are sometimes also those with the lowest levels of knowledge about the issue.
sentences.zh: 你还发现，对某个问题持有最强烈观点的人，有时也是对该问题了解水平最低的人。

sentences.en: Why would this be the case, Phil?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样，菲尔？

sentences.en: So I've studied this in the context of, um, controversial scientific issues.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在，嗯，有争议的科学问题背景下研究这个的。

sentences.en: So things like, um, the safety of genetically modified foods or the reality of climate change.
sentences.zh: 比如，嗯，转基因食品的安全性或气候变化的真实性。

sentences.en: Um, in those cases, there's a substantial minority of the population who expresses really extreme, strong counter consensus views.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在这些情况下，有一小部分人口表达了非常极端、强烈的反共识观点。

sentences.en: Um, views that are counter to the scientific consensus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些观点与科学共识背道而驰。

sentences.en: And what we find in that case is that the people who have the strongest, um, counter consensus views have the highest levels of subjective understanding.
sentences.zh: 我们在这种情况下发现的是，持有最强烈的、嗯，反共识观点的人，具有最高的主观理解水平。

sentences.en: They feel like they understand these issues the best, which makes sense because if I feel like I understand it really well, I'm going to have a strong opinion.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己对这些问题的理解最好，这很合理，因为如果我觉得自己理解得很好，我就会有强烈的意见。

sentences.en: But when we measure their actual understanding of the issue in a variety of ways, they actually have the lowest levels of objective knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但当我们通过各种方式衡量他们对该问题的实际理解时，他们实际上拥有最低水平的客观知识。

sentences.en: So when you put those things together,
sentences.zh: 所以当你把这些放在一起时，

sentences.en: the people who have the most extreme counter consensus views have this huge gap between what they think they know and what they actually know.
sentences.zh: 那些持有最极端的反共识观点的人，在他们认为自己知道的知识和他们实际知道的知识之间存在着巨大的差距。

sentences.en: Why do you think that's happening?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: The fact itself, of course, is striking and surprising, but is there a relationship between the two?
sentences.zh: 这个事实本身当然是惊人和令人惊讶的，但这两者之间存在某种联系吗？

sentences.en: Is the fact that they don't know partly what causes their certainty?
sentences.zh: 他们不知道的事实是否部分造成了他们的确定性？

sentences.en: I think that that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为是这样的。

sentences.en: Um, so if I feel like I understand something and I feel like I know it well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以如果我觉得我懂某件事，并且我觉得我对此很了解，

sentences.en: I'm going to be less likely to listen to counter evidence and counter explanations or to do more research into the issue to learn more about it.
sentences.zh: 我就不太可能去听取反面证据和反面解释，或者对这个问题做更多研究以了解更多信息。

sentences.en: If I already feel like I understand it, it's really hard to reach me with counter evidence.
sentences.zh: 如果我早就觉得我懂了，用反面证据来触动我就真的很困难。

sentences.en: And so the people whose views seem to be the most out of line with what the scientific community says are the ones who are hardest to reach because they already feel like they understand the issue.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些观点似乎最背离科学界说法的人，反而是最难触及的人，因为他们已经觉得自己理解这个问题了。

sentences.en: It turns out that many of the problems that beset us in the modern world have a common source.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，困扰现代社会的许多问题都有一个共同的根源。

sentences.en: We think we know something when actually we don't.
sentences.zh: 我们以为自己懂某事，而实际上并不懂。

sentences.en: When we come back, combating the knowledge illusion.
sentences.zh: 广告回来后，我们将探讨如何对抗知识错觉。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: Philip Fernbach is a cognitive scientist at the Leeds School of Business at the University of Colorado, Boulder.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·费恩巴赫是科罗拉多大学博尔德分校利兹商学院的认知科学家。

sentences.en: Phil, you say that in the face of the knowledge illusion,
sentences.zh: 菲尔，你说面对知识错觉，

sentences.en: one effective way to better align what we think we know with what we actually know is to challenge ourselves to explain technologies, procedures, and policies in our own words.
sentences.zh: 将我们以为自己知道的与我们实际知道的更好地结合起来的一个有效方法，是挑战自己用自己的话来解释技术、程序和政策。

sentences.en: Why does this dispel the knowledge illusion?
sentences.zh: 为什么这能消除知识错觉？

sentences.en: So we're not in the habit of engaging in a lot of explanation most of the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们大多数时候并没有进行大量解释的习惯。

sentences.en: We just take things for granted, as we've been discussing.
sentences.zh: 正如我们一直讨论的那样，我们只是把事情视为理所当然。

sentences.en: And so when we get in the habit of doing that, it's sort of hard to hide from ourselves that we don't understand things as well as we thought we did.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们养成这种习惯时，很难向自己隐瞒我们对事情的理解并不像我们想象的那么好。

sentences.en: A great example of this comes from work by Rebecca Lawson on people's understanding of bicycles.
sentences.zh: 这方面的一个极好的例子来自丽贝卡·劳森关于人们对自行车理解的研究。

sentences.en: So if you ask somebody, do you know how a bicycle works?
sentences.zh: 如果你问某人，你知道自行车是怎么运作的吗？

sentences.en: A lot of people say, oh yeah, I kind of know how that works.
sentences.zh: 很多人会说，哦，是的，我大概知道它是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: But then in the study, what she did was she asked people to draw a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 但随后在这项研究中，她所做的是要求人们画一辆自行车。

sentences.en: And if you sit down and try to do it, I encourage the listeners to try to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你坐下来尝试去画，我鼓励听众们也试着去画一下。

sentences.en: It's much more difficult than you might have anticipated.
sentences.zh: 这比你预期的要困难得多。

sentences.en: And that's just a great example of, in that case, it's impossible to hide from yourself the gaps in your knowledge.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的例子，在这种情况下，你不可能向自己隐瞒知识中的空白。

sentences.en: They've just become revealed on the page as you try to draw.
sentences.zh: 当你试图画画时，它们刚巧就在纸上显露出来了。

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, this is not hugely different from what happens in a school setting where you're giving a student a test and you're basically saying,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些方面，这与学校里发生的情况没有太大区别，在那里你给学生一场考试，你基本上是在说，

sentences.en: produce for me your knowledge.
sentences.zh: 向我展示你的知识。

sentences.en: You know, you think that you know how differential equations work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你以为你知道微分方程是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Produce for me that knowledge by solving this problem.
sentences.zh: 通过解决这个问题向我展示你的知识。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A test that is designed to actually gauge understanding of the way things work, as opposed to a test that is merely regurgitating facts.
sentences.zh: 一场旨在真正评估对事物运作方式理解的考试，而不是仅仅死记硬背事实的考试。

sentences.en: So a test that's well designed to actually evaluate whether somebody understands the details or mechanisms of the way that something works would indeed reveal those gaps.
sentences.zh: 因此，一场设计得当、旨在真正评估某人是否理解事物运作细节或机制的考试，确实会暴露出这些差距。

sentences.en: I have a colleague who was recently telling me a story about one of his classes where he was just imploring students,
sentences.zh: 我有一位同事最近跟我讲了他某个班级的故事，当时他正恳求学生们，

sentences.en: if you are using artificial intelligence to try to help you with the class, make sure that you understand this and not just are using the artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在使用人工智能来帮助你完成课程，请确保你理解了这一点，而不只是在使用人工智能。

sentences.en: And yet, when the test came around and they'd all been using chat GPT,
sentences.zh: 然而，当测试到来时，他们都使用了 ChatGPT，

sentences.en: they learned that they did not understand the material as well as they thought that they did because they had been relying on the artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 他们了解到，他们对材料的理解并没有自己想象的那么好，因为他们一直依赖人工智能。

sentences.en: And they got very upset with him.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And he sort of explained to them, look, I tried to tell you,
sentences.zh: 他向他们解释说，听着，我试着告诉过你们，

sentences.en: but this is such a natural human thing to overestimate our understanding that it's very hard to actually appreciate the gaps in our knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但高估自己的理解力是人类非常自然的天性，以至于很难真正意识到我们知识中的盲区。

sentences.en: We often, it's so natural for us to go through life just not really questioning and assuming we know more than we do that we don't really see it.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，我们在生活中顺其自然，不去真正质疑，并认为自己懂得比实际更多，以至于我们没有真正看到这一点。

sentences.en: And that's why getting into this habit of questioning yourself and questioning your understanding is a very powerful tool for dispelling the illusion.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么养成质疑自己、质疑自己理解的习惯是消除这种错觉的强大工具。

sentences.en: So you've asked people with strong views on political issues to explain public policies in detail.
sentences.zh: 所以，你曾让对政治问题有强烈观点的人详细解释公共政策。

sentences.en: What effect does this have on their certainties, Phil?
sentences.zh: 菲尔，这对他们的确定性有什么影响？

sentences.en: So in our studies, we've often compared two different types of explanations.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的研究中，我们经常比较两种不同类型的解释。

sentences.en: One is this mechanistic explanation, how does it work?
sentences.zh: 一种是这种机制性的解释，它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: And the other is more about why you believe what you do.
sentences.zh: 另一种更多地关于你为什么相信你所相信的。

sentences.en: So reasons.
sentences.zh: 也就是理由。

sentences.en: And you can think about those two modes of thinking as being more explanatory or mechanistic on the one hand, and then more argumentative or advocacy-based on the other hand.
sentences.zh: 你可以把这两种思维模式看作一方面是解释性或机制性的，另一方面是论证性或倡导性的。

sentences.en: I think we are much more commonly engaged in this argumentation or advocacy when we're talking about things like political issues.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当我们谈论政治问题之类的事情时，更多地参与这种争论或倡导。

sentences.en: We very rarely engage in this kind of mechanistic or explanatory kind of discussion.
sentences.zh: 我们极少参与这种机制性或解释性的讨论。

sentences.en: But it turns out that the mechanistic or explanatory mode leads to a little more open-mindedness.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，机制性或解释性的模式会带来更多的开放包容。

sentences.en: It gets people to be a little less certain about their positions because it reveals the complexity of issues.
sentences.zh: 它让人对自己的立场不那么确定，因为它揭示了问题的复杂性。

sentences.en: And this has been demonstrated to some extent in our work where we simply ask people,
sentences.zh: 我们的工作在某种程度上证明了这一点，我们只是问人们，

sentences.en: well, how do you feel about these issues afterwards?
sentences.zh: 嗯，事后你对这些问题有什么感觉？

sentences.en: But I think even more interestingly and meaningfully, there was a great paper by Elna Corey Hunn and Grossman a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 但我认为更有趣、更有意义的是，几年前埃尔娜·科里·亨恩和格罗斯曼写了一篇很棒的论文。

sentences.en: And they asked people on different sides of the political divide to have political discussions.
sentences.zh: 他们让政治分歧两端的人进行政治讨论。

sentences.en: And then they measured different things about the discussion,
sentences.zh: 然后他们衡量了关于讨论的不同方面，

sentences.en: like how well it went and how open-minded people seemed to be and how much they were listening to the other side and those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 比如讨论进展得如何、人们显得多么开放、他们能在多大程度上倾听另一方的意见之类的事情。

sentences.en: And what they found is that the discussions were more productive when people engaged in this more explanatory kind of discussion.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，当人们参与这种更具解释性的讨论时，讨论会更富有成效。

sentences.en: Did you find that when people are asked to engage in this more explanatory style of conversation,
sentences.zh: 你是否发现，当人们被要求参与这种更具解释性的对话风格时，

sentences.en: that political polarization goes down because some of people's political certainties go down?
sentences.zh: 由于人们的一些政治确定性下降，政治极化也会下降？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They move to the middle a little bit.
sentences.zh: 他们稍微向中间靠拢了一点。

sentences.en: The challenge with that is that people get defensive as well.
sentences.zh: 这样做面临的挑战是，人们也会产生防御心理。

sentences.en: So if you challenge people with their understanding, they might actually double down and say,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你用他们的理解去挑战他们，他们实际上可能会加倍坚持并说，

sentences.en: no, I know what I'm talking about because people naturally tend to be a little bit defensive.
sentences.zh: 不，我知道我在说什么，因为人们天生倾向于有一点防御心理。

sentences.en: So the way to actually implement such an intervention can be a little bit challenging in its details because, again, human beings are not simple.
sentences.zh: 因此，实际实施这种干预的方法在细节上可能有点挑战性，因为同样，人类并不简单。

sentences.en: They're complex.
sentences.zh: 他们很复杂。

sentences.en: So if you reveal people's lack of understanding to them, it may have the effect of making them a little bit more humble or more moderate,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你向人们揭示他们缺乏理解，可能会起到让他们变得更加谦逊或温和的作用，

sentences.en: but it could also make them double down on their position a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但也可能让他们更加固执己见。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether you might have advice for people who are sitting across the table with a friend or family member with whom they're having a really strenuous disagreement or debate.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，对于那些与朋友或家人坐在一起，并且正在进行激烈争论或辩论的人，你有什么建议吗？

sentences.en: How would you encourage them to invite the other person to engage in explanatory thinking as opposed to argumentative thinking?
sentences.zh: 你会如何鼓励他们邀请对方进行解释性思考，而不是争论性思考？

sentences.en: The key is to be curious about the other side's position.
sentences.zh: 关键是要对另一方的立场保持好奇心。

sentences.en: So if you start from a perspective of the other side is not as smart as me, is not as ethical or moral as me, they're bad, they're stupid,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你从“对方不如我聪明、不如我有道德、他们很坏、他们很愚蠢”的视角出发，

sentences.en: then you're not going to be likely to have a very productive discussion.
sentences.zh: 那么你就不太可能进行非常有成效的讨论。

sentences.en: If you start instead with the perspective of the person that I'm talking to is as smart as me and as moral as me, then you become curious.
sentences.zh: 相反，如果你从“我交谈的人和我一样聪明、和我一样有道德”的视角出发，你就会产生好奇心。

sentences.en: Why is it that they maintain a strong position that's so different from yours when it seems like the right answer is just so obvious to you?
sentences.zh: 为什么在你看来正确答案如此显而易见的时候，他们却坚持与你如此不同的强硬立场？

sentences.en: And then when you become curious and if both sides are mutually curious and they want to understand what is behind the other side's position,
sentences.zh: 然后，当你产生好奇心，如果双方都对彼此感到好奇，并且想要了解对方立场背后的原因，

sentences.en: then you can have a more productive discussion.
sentences.zh: 那么你们就能进行更富有成效的讨论。

sentences.en: And I think what you will find is that when you engage jointly in this explanatory kind of discussion, it's more of a collaboration than it is an argument.
sentences.zh: 我想你会发现，当你共同参与这种解释性的讨论时，与其说是一场争论，不如说是一次合作。

sentences.en: And that collaboration is going to reveal likely that both sides don't know as much as they thought they did at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这种合作可能会揭示，双方并不像他们最初认为的那样了解那么多。

sentences.en: That's going to be the most common outcome.
sentences.zh: 这将是最常见的结果。

sentences.en: I mean, I think one thing that I take away from that is that even when we encounter people with beliefs that are very different from our own,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为从中汲取的一点是，即使我们遇到与我们有很大不同信念的人，

sentences.en: or even beliefs that we can prove are certifiably wrong, perhaps the right response actually is some degree of compassion.
sentences.zh: 甚至是我们能证明明显错误的信念，也许正确的反应实际上某种程度上是同情。

sentences.en: Because in some ways, I think what I hear you saying is that the process by which they are arriving at their erroneous beliefs
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，我认为我听到你所说的是，他们得出错误信念的过程

sentences.en: is not different than the process at which I arrive at what might be correct beliefs.
sentences.zh: 与我得出可能是正确信念的过程并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: I agree with that 100 percent because we all have beliefs that are incorrect.
sentences.zh: 我百分之百同意这一点，因为我们所有人都有不正确的信念。

sentences.en: And we all have beliefs that we have much more strength and conviction in than we should.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人持有的信念，其坚定和确信程度都超过了我们应有的水平。

sentences.en: And conspiracies are a bizarre sort of extreme example of this,
sentences.zh: 阴谋论是一个奇怪的极端例子，

sentences.en: but they're part and parcel of the same kind of mechanisms that lead to all of our beliefs.
sentences.zh: 但它们与导致我们所有信念的各种机制密不可分。

sentences.en: So, another way to better grasp what we don't know is to engage in a practice of considering the unknowns.
sentences.zh: 因此，更好地掌握我们所不知道的事物的另一种方法是实践考虑未知事物。

sentences.en: What is this practice, Phil?
sentences.zh: 菲尔，这种实践是什么？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, there's been a lot of research in the psychology literature on overconfidence.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学文献中有大量关于过度自信的研究。

sentences.en: People tend to be overconfident in a lot of different ways.
sentences.zh: 人们在很多不同的方面往往过于自信。

sentences.en: The reason for overconfidence is what's called confirmation bias.
sentences.zh: 过度自信的原因被称为确认偏误。

sentences.en: That is, we're preferentially disposed to find evidence for the position that we start with, the one that we want.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们倾向于寻找证据来支持我们最初的立场，即我们想要的立场。

sentences.en: Some of the work that I've done is looking at another reason that we're overconfident.
sentences.zh: 我做过的一些工作是研究我们过度自信的另一个原因。

sentences.en: It's not just because we tend to preferentially weight the evidence for our positions,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为我们倾向于赋予支持我们立场的证据更多权重，

sentences.en: but also that we tend to neglect all of the unknown information.
sentences.zh: 还因为我们倾向于忽视所有未知的信息。

sentences.en: And that's part and parcel of all of the themes that we've been talking about today,
sentences.zh: 这与我们今天一直在讨论的所有主题息息相关，

sentences.en: that the world just seems simpler than it is.
sentences.zh: 即世界似乎比实际情况更简单。

sentences.en: If the world seems simpler and we're confronted with an issue,
sentences.zh: 如果世界看起来更简单，而我们又面临一个问题，

sentences.en: then we're going to tend not to think about all of the stuff that we don't know.
sentences.zh: 那么我们往往不会去思考所有我们不知道的事情。

sentences.en: We're going to tend to think about the stuff that we do know.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会去思考我们确实知道的事情。

sentences.en: And if we thought about all the stuff that we don't know,
sentences.zh: 如果我们去思考所有我们不知道的事情，

sentences.en: it would make us more moderate in our positions because,
sentences.zh: 这会让我们在自己的立场上变得更加温和，因为，

sentences.en: wow, there's a lot more to know about this.
sentences.zh: 哇，关于这个还有很多需要了解的地方。

sentences.en: There is another dimension of the illusion of knowledge that affects organizations and groups.
sentences.zh: 知识的错觉还有一个维度，它会影响组织和群体。

sentences.en: And it affects us when we are part of large groups.
sentences.zh: 当我们成为大群体的一部分时，它也会影响我们。

sentences.en: This aspect of the illusion of knowledge shapes gyrations in the stock market
sentences.zh: 知识错觉的这一方面塑造了股市的波动

sentences.en: and your retirement portfolio.
sentences.zh: 以及你的退休投资组合。

sentences.en: What we find is that when people search the internet for financial information,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当人们在互联网上搜索财务信息时，

sentences.en: they become overconfident in their knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们对自己知识的信心会过度膨胀。

sentences.en: And not only do they become overconfident in their knowledge,
sentences.zh: 他们不仅对自己的知识过于自信，

sentences.en: but that leads to downstream behaviors like taking on more risk.
sentences.zh: 这还会导致后续行为，例如承担更多风险。

sentences.en: Our story comes from Cara Beth Rogers.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事来自卡拉·贝丝·罗杰斯（Cara Beth Rogers）。

sentences.en: In 2008, Cara Beth's brother, Luke, passed away unexpectedly.
sentences.zh: 2008年，卡拉·贝丝的弟弟卢克不幸离世。

sentences.en: Cara Beth was 20 years old at the time, studying abroad in Morocco.
sentences.zh: 当时卡拉·贝丝20岁，正在摩洛哥留学。

sentences.en: The shock of the news made it nearly impossible for her to form a sentence,
sentences.zh: 突如其来的打击让她几乎无法组织语言，

sentences.en: let alone fly all the way back to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 更不用说一路飞回美国了。

sentences.en: She managed to get to the airport, but as soon as she boarded the plane,
sentences.zh: 她设法赶到了机场，但一登上飞机，

sentences.en: the grief became unbearable.
sentences.zh: 悲伤就变得让人无法承受。

sentences.en: I was sitting on an aisle, and I will never forget the way that it felt to try to sit still.
sentences.zh: 我坐在过道座位上，我永远不会忘记努力坐着不动时的那种感觉。

sentences.en: It was impossible.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的。

sentences.en: I couldn't stop moving.
sentences.zh: 我无法停止颤抖或移动。

sentences.en: The strength of the emotions was so intense.
sentences.zh: 情绪的力量太强烈了。

sentences.en: I really stood out, and I felt like people were avoiding eye contact with me.
sentences.zh: 我真的很显眼，我感觉人们都在避免与我目光接触。

sentences.en: They weren't really sure what to do with me.
sentences.zh: 他们真的不知道该怎么对待我。

sentences.en: And partway through the flight, this man came up to me.
sentences.zh: 在飞行途中，这个男人朝我走了过来。

sentences.en: I was sitting on the aisle on the right side of the plane,
sentences.zh: 我坐在飞机右侧的过道座位上，

sentences.en: so he came up to me, and he crouched down next to me on my left side.
sentences.zh: 所以他走过来，在我左侧蹲了下去。

sentences.en: And he was so gentle.
sentences.zh: 他是那么温和。

sentences.en: He made direct eye contact with me, and he spoke softly and slowly,
sentences.zh: 他直接看着我的眼睛，轻声而缓慢地说话，

sentences.en: and he was really sincere.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常真诚。

sentences.en: And he said, I know you don't know me, and I don't know what's going on for you,
sentences.zh: 他说，我知道你不认识我，我也不知道你经历了什么，

sentences.en: but I want you to know that if you need anything, I'm here.
sentences.zh: 但我希望你知道，如果你需要任何东西，我都在。

sentences.en: And I said, thank you.
sentences.zh: 我说，谢谢你。

sentences.en: I never ended up going to him during that flight, but knowing he saw me.
sentences.zh: 在那次飞行中我最终没有去找他，但知道他看到了我。

sentences.en: You know, I felt like I was in this cavern of just, like, untenable emotion
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得自己身处一个充满无法承受的情绪的深渊中，

sentences.en: and that I was deeply, deeply alone.
sentences.zh: 而且我感到无比的孤独。

sentences.en: And, you know, having lost a brother, we were so close in age.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，失去了弟弟，我们年龄相仿。

sentences.en: We grew up just one year in school apart,
sentences.zh: 我们在学校只差一个年级，一同长大，

sentences.en: and knowing that I was on a plane with somebody that could see me
sentences.zh: 知道飞机上有这样一个人，他能看到我，

sentences.en: and that knew that I needed something,
sentences.zh: 并且知道我需要帮助，

sentences.en: even if I didn't know what it was, even if they didn't know what it was,
sentences.zh: 即使我不知道那是什么，即使他们不知道那是什么，

sentences.en: was an incredibly powerful experience.
sentences.zh: 也是一次极其震撼的体验。

sentences.en: I will forever be grateful for him.
sentences.zh: 我将永远对他心存感激。

sentences.en: It was a really powerful moment for me.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，这是一个非常震撼的时刻。
